definitions.explanation: The hour four on the clock. Note the irregular reading よ, not し or よん, before the counter {時|じ}.

examples.japanese: {四時|よじ}に{会|あ}いましょう。
{午後|ごご}{四時|よじ}{半|はん}に{電話|でんわ}します。
examples.english: I'll call at four thirty in the afternoon.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}{四時|よじ}に{起|お}きて、{始発|しはつ}の{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}るつもりだ。
examples.english: I plan to get up at four tomorrow morning and take the first train.

notes:
One of the three irregular hour readings that learners must memorize.

IRREGULAR HOUR READINGS:
- {四時|よじ}: four o'clock — よ, not し or よん
- {七時|しちじ}: seven o'clock — しち (しちじ is standard; ななじ is heard but non-standard)
- {九時|くじ}: nine o'clock — く, not きゅう

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {四時|よじ}{半|はん}: half past four
- {午前|ごぜん}{四時|よじ}: four a.m.
- {四時|よじ}から: from four o'clock

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {四分|よんぷん}: four minutes — the minute counter takes よん, not よ
